header_desc_1: DarkMoon Engine is a graphics engine built from scratch in C++23 and OpenGL. It started as the backbone for Two Wonders, built to handle the project's technical needs without falling apart under complex scenes.
header_desc_2: This new version is focused exclusively on 2D, with a cleaner and more modular architecture than its predecessor. The original code was refactored top to bottom to make everything easier to understand, extend, and maintain.
header_ecs: Entity Component System built on a custom SlotMap and compile-time type metaprogramming. Header-only, no dynamic allocations, and designed for you to instantiate with your own types.
whatis_desc: ECS is a pattern that separates data (components) from logic (systems), using lightweight IDs (entities) to connect them.
whatis_core_entity: Entity: a numeric ID with a bitmask that tracks which components and tags it owns. No data of its own.
whatis_core_component: Component: a plain data struct (e.g. PhysicsComponent, RenderComponent). No logic, no weird inheritance.
whatis_core_tag: Tag: an empty struct that acts as a boolean flag (e.g. TagPlayer, TagEnemy). Takes up nothing in the SlotMap.
whatis_core_system: System: a struct with an update(EM&, ...) method that loops over entities and does things with their components.
whatis_core_em: Entity Manager: the core. Owns all entities and their component storage. You instantiate it with your own types.
whatis_design_headeronly: Header-only, all of it. Everything lives in .hpp files because it's template-based, and that makes it much easier to drop into any project.
whatis_design_slotmap: Each component type gets its own SlotMap, giving O(1) access and cache-friendly iteration.
whatis_design_bitmask: Bitmasks are resolved at compile time via MP::cmp_tag_traits. No type lookups at runtime.
whatis_design_limits: Defaults are 200 entities and 350 slots per SlotMap. Both are template parameters, so you can change them.
whatis_design_types: You define CMPList and TAGList in types.hpp. The engine doesn't assume anything about your types.
architecture_desc: DarkMoon resolves everything at compile time. You define which components and tags exist, and the engine builds on top of that with no runtime overhead.
architecture_dataflow_desc: Everything starts from types.hpp. From there you instantiate the EntityManager and you're good to go create entities, add components, run queries, and iterate with lambdas.
typeshpp_desc: types.hpp is the file you have to create and edit when you add components or tags. This is where you instantiate the EntityManager with your concrete types.
architecture_types_reminder: Don't forget to add every new component or tag to CMPList / TAGList in types.hpp. If you skip this, the EntityManager won't know they exist.
components_desc: Components are plain data structs. No logic, no weird methods, just data.
components_list_1: They must be default-constructible that's a SlotMap requirement.
components_list_2: Keep them small and focused. One component, one thing.
components_list_3: They can hold heap data via std::unique_ptr, but watch out for move semantics when the SlotMap reorganizes storage.
tags_desc: Tags are empty structs that work as boolean flags. They only take up a single bit in the entity's bitmask and don't allocate any slot in the SlotMap.
systems_desc: Systems are structs with an update() method that takes the EM by reference. They use forEach to iterate only the entities they care about.
systems_callout: Declare SYSCMPs and SYSTAGs as aliases inside the struct. It makes the system self-documenting and future-you will be grateful.
entities_api_desc: How to create, look up, and destroy entities.
api_newEntity: Creates a new entity and returns a reference to it. Hits an assert if you reach MAX_ENTITIES (200).
api_destroyEntityByID: Destroys the entity with that ID and all its components. Uses swap-with-last internally so it's O(1).
api_destroyEntities: Batch-destroys a set of entities. The set must be sorted in descending order (std::greater) to avoid index invalidation mid-removal.
api_destroyAll: Wipes everything entities and component storages. Clean slate.
api_getEntityByID: Returns a pointer to the entity with that ID, or nullptr if it doesn't exist. Linear search, don't call this every frame.
api_getEntities: Returns a span over all currently alive entities. Safe to iterate as long as you're not destroying entities in the middle of it.
api_aliveCount: How many entities are alive right now.
api_freeEntities: How many more entities you can create before hitting MAX_ENTITIES.
api_entity_getID: The unique ID of this entity. Assigned sequentially and never reused within a session.
api_entity_hasComponent: Returns true if the entity owns a component of type T. Bitmask check: O(1).
api_entity_hasTag: Returns true if the entity has that tag. Bitmask check: O(1).
components_api_desc: Adding, accessing, and removing components and tags on entities.
api_addComponent: Adds a component of type T to entity e, forwarding args to its constructor. If the entity already has that component, returns the existing one without creating a new one.
api_getComponent: Returns a reference to the component of type T on entity e. Asserts if the entity does not have that component, always check with hasComponent first if unsure.
api_destroyComponent: Removes the component of type T from entity e and frees its slot in the SlotMap. No-op if the entity does not have that component.
api_addTag: Sets the tag bit for type T on entity e. Tags have no storage, only the bitmask bit is flipped.
api_destroyTag: Clears the tag bit for type T on entity e.
section_iteration_desc: Iterating entities that match a set of required components and tags.
api_forEach: Calls func(Entity&, CMP&...) for every alive entity that has all components in CMPs and all tags in TAGs. The component references are passed as arguments to the lambda in the same order as CMPs.
api_forEachAny: Calls func(Entity&) for every entity that has any component in CMPs or any tag in TAGs. No component references are passed use getComponent inside the lambda.
slotmap_desc: Each component type gets its own Slotmap<T, Capacity> instance inside the EntityManager. The SlotMap provides O(1) insert, erase, and lookup while keeping all live data packed contiguously in memory - critical for cache performance during forEach iteration.
slotmap_param_capacity: Maximum number of elements. Fixed at compile-time; set via MAX_ENTITIES in types.hpp.
slotmap_param_indext: Integer type used for indices and generations. Use uint16_t to reduce memory on small worlds.
slotmap_arrays_desc: Three fixed-size arrays work together to provide stable keys over a packed data buffer.
slotmap_key_desc: A key_type is a small POD pair returned by push_back. The generation field makes stale-key detection free - no extra bookkeeping required at the call site.
slotmap_api_push_move: Insert by move. Throws std::runtime_error if full.
slotmap_api_push_copy: Insert by copy (delegates to move overload).
slotmap_api_access: Unchecked access. Asserts validity in debug builds.
slotmap_api_erase: Remove element. Returns false if key is already invalid.
slotmap_api_isvalid: Check whether a key still refers to a live element.
slotmap_api_clear: Reset all slots and reinitialise the freelist.
slotmap_api_iter: Raw iterators over the packed data range [0, size).
slotmap_swappop_desc: When an element is erased and it is not the last one in m_data, the last element is moved into the freed slot. Three pointer fixups keep everything consistent:
slotmap_swappop_after: The slot for B is returned to the freelist and its generation is bumped. Any stored key_type for B now fails is_valid() because m_indices[b].gen != key.gen.
slotmap_callout: The EntityManager stores one Slotmap<CMP, MAX_ENTITIES> per component type in a std::tuple. Access is via std::get<Index>(m_slotmaps), where the index is resolved at compile-time through MP::IndexOf.
metaprog_desc: All compile-time logic lives in the MP:: namespace inside meta_program.hpp. It is a self-contained, zero-dependency header that reimplements the type-traits machinery needed by EntityManager without relying on <type_traits>. Every facility is consteval or resolved at compile-time - no runtime cost.
metaprog_foundational_desc: The header starts by defining its own Boolean and value constants, keeping the namespace self-contained.
metaprog_nth_title: nth_type - index into a parameter pack
metaprog_nth_desc: Extracts the N-th type from a variadic pack via recursive specialisation. Used internally by TypeList and cmp_tag_traits.
metaprog_pos_desc: Walks the pack at compile-time and returns the zero-based index of T. Triggers a static assert if T is not present.
metaprog_ift_desc: Selects between two types based on a boolean condition. Equivalent to std::conditional. Used by smallest_type to pick the narrowest integer that fits the bitmask.
metaprog_typelist_desc: The main user-facing type. A variadic struct with no data members - pure compile-time information. Exposes three consteval member functions.
metaprog_smallest_desc: Given a TypeList, selects the narrowest unsigned integer that can hold one bit per type. This is the mask_type used by every entity to store its component/tag bitmask.
metaprog_smallest_callout: The maximum combined total of components + tags is 64, enforced by a static_assert inside cmp_tag_traits. Exceeding this limit is a compile error.
metaprog_traits_desc: The central metaprogramming type consumed by EntityManager. Given the full merged TypeList of all components and tags, it exposes the mask_type and the consteval mask() function used to build query masks at compile-time.
metaprog_traits_callout: An empty TypeList<> specialisation of cmp_tag_traits is provided so that passing an empty component or tag list to forEach always compiles cleanly and produces a mask of 0 (matches everything).
metaprog_transformers_desc: Two additional helpers allow reusing a TypeList with different wrappers, used internally to build the std::tuple of SlotMaps.
metaprog_foreachtuple_desc: A runtime helper that calls a lambda on every element of a std::tuple, iterating by index via template recursion. Used by EntityManager to reset all SlotMaps on destroyAll() and to build bitmask queries that touch each component storage in turn.
metaprog_ref_constant: Holds a single compile-time value V of type T.
metaprog_ref_nth: Extracts the N-th type from a parameter pack.
metaprog_ref_smallest: Narrowest uintN_t that fits one bit per type in TL.
metaprog_ref_foreachtuple: Calls f(element) for every element of a std::tuple.
iteration_callout: Do not call destroyEntityByID() or destroyEntities() from inside a forEach lambda. Collect IDs into a deathSet during iteration and destroy them after the loop.
example1_desc: Create an entity, add a component, retrieve it, and query its existence. This is the minimal lifecycle every ECS interaction is built on: newEntity → addComponent → getComponent → hasComponent.
example2_desc: One entity can carry any subset of the registered components. Shows how to compose a player (Position + Velocity + Health), a static enemy (Position + Health), and a pickup (Position only), then how forEach filters strictly by intersection - only entities that own every requested component are visited.
example3_desc: Tags are empty structs that consume a single bitmask bit and no SlotMap slot. This example uses TagPlayer, TagEnemy, and TagInvincible to categorize entities and gate damage logic - including adding and removing TagInvincible at runtime to simulate a power-up effect.
example4_desc: Three systems (MovementSystem, BoundsSystem, CombatSystem) each declare their own SYSCMPs / SYSTAGs and expose a single update(EM&) method. The main loop owns only the EntityManager and calls the systems in order every frame, keeping game logic fully decoupled from data.
example5_desc: Destroying entities inside a forEach corrupts iteration. The correct pattern is to collect IDs into an EM::deathSet during the loop and call destroyEntities afterwards - and destroyAll for scene resets.
example6_desc: forEach requires an entity to match all requested components and tags (AND). forEachAny visits if it matches at least one of the requested tags (OR). The example builds four entities with different component and tag combinations, then runs several queries to show exactly which entities each overload selects and why.
header_window: Window management, OpenGL context, input and timing on top of GLFW.
window_whatis_desc: Window is the central class of the DarkMoon Engine graphics module. It encapsulates GLFW window creation, GLAD initialization, basic shader loading, the drawing loop, the input system (keyboard, mouse and gamepad) and FPS control.
window_feat_lifecycle: Automatic GLFW window creation and destruction.
window_feat_drawing: BeginDrawing / EndDrawing with precision busy-wait FPS cap.
window_feat_input: Keyboard and mouse input with per-frame states (Pressed / Down / Released / Up).
window_feat_shaders: Automatic loading of basic 2D shaders on window construction.
window_feat_fps: DeltaTime and FPS counter updated on every EndDrawing.
window_feat_modes: Windowed, Borderless and Fullscreen modes with automatic size/position restoration.
window_mode_desc: The WindowMode enum controls the display mode of the window. It can be changed at runtime with SetWindowMode(), SetFullscreen(), SetBorderless() or SetWindowed().
window_setup_desc: GLFW must be initialized once before creating any Window. The constructor handles everything else: creating the window, loading GLAD (first window only) and compiling the basic shaders. When the Window object is destroyed, the window closes automatically.
window_setup_callout: Create DarkMoonEngine before constructing any Window and glfwTerminate() when exiting the program. Do not call glfwDestroyWindow() manually; the Window destructor handles it.
lifecycle_desc: Methods for controlling the window state: visibility, focus, minimize and maximize.
api_win_ctor: Creates the GLFW window, initializes GLAD and loads the basic shaders. If sharedContext is provided, shares the OpenGL context with that window.
api_win_close: Marks the window to close on the next ShouldClose() call.
api_win_shouldclose: Returns true if the window should close (exit key pressed or close button clicked).
api_win_iconify: Minimizes the window to the taskbar.
api_win_maximize: Maximizes the window to fill the desktop.
api_win_restore: Restores the window to its previous size and position.
api_win_hide: Hides the window without destroying it.
api_win_show: Shows the window and restores its saved position and size.
api_win_focus: Brings the window to the front and gives it keyboard focus.
api_win_current: Makes this window's OpenGL context current on the calling thread.
api_win_wasresized: Returns true if the window size has changed, or false otherwise.
drawing_desc: The DarkMoon drawing loop follows the BeginDrawing / EndDrawing pattern. BeginDrawing sets up the orthographic projection and clears the background. EndDrawing applies the FPS cap, computes deltaTime, processes events and swaps buffers.
drawing_loop_desc: Every frame follows this order. Do not render outside this block.
api_begin_drawing: Sets up the orthographic projection and viewport. Does not clear the background.
api_begin_drawing_color: Same as BeginDrawing() but also clears the background with the given color.
api_end_drawing: Applies the FPS cap (busy-wait), updates deltaTime, calls PollEvents() and swaps buffers.
api_end_drawing_nopoll: Same as EndDrawing() but skips glfwPollEvents(). Useful in multi-window setups.
api_clear_background: Clears the color and depth buffer with the given color.
shaders_desc: Window automatically loads three basic shaders on construction. You can retrieve them via getters or create custom shaders from file paths or inline GLSL source strings.
shaders_builtin_desc: Compiled automatically in the constructor. Available immediately after creating the window.
api_shader_basic: Solid color shader. Accepts uniform vec4 customColor. No textures or UV coordinates.
api_shader_texture: Textured shader with per-vertex color. Inputs: aPos, aColor, aTextCoord. uniform sampler2D texture1.
api_shader_font: Font rendering shader. Reads the R channel of the atlas as alpha. uniform sampler2D uAtlas + customColor.
api_shader_create_path: Loads and compiles a shader from file paths. The geometry shader parameter is optional.
api_shader_create_src: Compiles a shader directly from GLSL source strings. Useful for shaders embedded in the executable.
shaders_callout: CreateShader() calls Current() internally to ensure the correct context is active before compiling. You do not need to call it manually.
input_api_desc: The input system is updated on every PollEvents() call (called internally by EndDrawing). States compare the current and previous frame to provide four detection levels per key and mouse button.
input_keyboard_desc: Use the KEY_* constants from darkmoon/utils/keys.hpp. The default exit key is KEY_ESCAPE; releasing it closes the window automatically.
api_key_pressed: True only on the frame the key transitions from not-pressed to pressed.
api_key_released: True only on the frame the key is released.
api_key_down: True every frame the key is held (including the first frame).
api_key_up: True every frame the key is NOT pressed.
api_key_lastchar: Last Unicode character received via the char callback. Useful for text input fields.
api_key_exitkey: Sets the key that closes the window when released. Default is KEY_ESCAPE.
api_poll_events: Updates input states and calls glfwPollEvents(). EndDrawing() calls this automatically.
api_mouse_pressed: True only on the frame the button transitions to pressed.
api_mouse_released: True only on the frame the button is released.
api_mouse_down: True every frame the button is held.
api_mouse_up: True every frame the button is NOT pressed.
api_cursor_pos: Cursor position in screen pixels as Vector2Df.
api_cursor_setpos: Moves the cursor to the given position as Vector2Df.
api_cursor_setx: Moves the cursor to the given X coordinate.
api_cursor_sety: Moves the cursor to the given Y coordinate.
api_scroll_x: Horizontal scroll wheel offset for the current frame.
api_scroll_y: Vertical scroll wheel offset for the current frame. Positive = scroll up.
api_cursor_hover: True if the cursor is over the window's client area.
api_cursor_disable: Hides and captures the cursor inside the window (FPS mode). GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED.
api_cursor_hide: Hides the cursor visually without capturing it. GLFW_CURSOR_HIDDEN.
api_cursor_enable: Restores the cursor to normal visible mode. GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL.
api_cursor_custom: Loads a PNG image (recommended size 16x16x4) and sets it as the cursor.
api_cursor_reset: Restores the cursor to the system's standard arrow pointer.
window_api_desc: Methods for controlling and querying window properties: size, position, mode, title, icon and opacity.
api_win_fullscreen: Switches to exclusive fullscreen mode. Saves the windowed size and position for later restoration.
api_win_borderless: Switches to borderless fullscreen. Covers the entire screen without changing the output resolution.
api_win_windowed: Restores windowed mode to the size and position saved before the last mode change.
api_win_mode: Changes the window mode using the WindowMode enum. Equivalent to calling SetFullscreen / SetBorderless / SetWindowed.
api_win_setsize: Sets the window size in pixels. Only takes effect in Windowed mode.
api_win_setsize_v: Same as SetSize(w, h) but accepts a Vector2Df.
api_win_setpos: Moves the window to the given screen coordinates. Windowed mode only.
api_win_setpos_v: Same as SetPosition(x, y) but accepts a Vector2Df.
api_win_settitle: Changes the text of the window title bar.
api_win_seticon: Loads a PNG image and sets it as the window icon (taskbar and title bar).
api_win_seticondefault: Sets the default icon as the window icon (taskbar and title bar).
api_win_setopacity: Sets the window opacity. Range 0.0 (transparent) to 1.0 (opaque).
window_api_setsize_setpos_callout: SetSize() and SetPosition() only take effect in WindowMode::Windowed. Calls made in Fullscreen or Borderless mode are ignored.
api_win_getmode: Returns the current WindowMode: Windowed, Borderless or Fullscreen.
api_win_getwindow: Returns the raw GLFWwindow* pointer for direct use with the GLFW API.
api_win_getposx: X coordinate of the window's top-left corner on the desktop.
api_win_getposy: Y coordinate of the window's top-left corner on the desktop.
api_win_getpos: Window position on the desktop as Vector2Df.
fps_api_desc: DarkMoon uses a busy-wait FPS cap for higher precision than a pure sleep. DeltaTime is updated at the start of EndDrawing and should be used to scale any time-dependent speed or animation.
fps_internal_desc: EndDrawing executes the following steps in order:
api_fps_settarget: Sets the target FPS. Pass 0 to disable the cap (uncapped speed).
api_fps_get: Returns the measured FPS averaged over the last 100 ms interval.
api_fps_delta: Time in seconds since the previous frame. Use it for framerate-independent movement.
api_fps_time: Time in seconds since GLFW was initialized. Equivalent to glfwGetTime().
misc_api_desc: Additional utilities for accessing the system clipboard and detecting files dragged onto the window.
api_clipboard_get: Returns the current system clipboard content as a C string. May be nullptr.
api_clipboard_set: Writes the given string to the system clipboard.
api_drop_set: Registers a callback function called whenever the user drags files onto the window.
api_drop_getpath: Returns the path of the last dropped file. Empty string if none.
api_drop_isfile: True if there is at least one pending path to process (GetLastDroppedPath is not empty).
api_drop_clear: Clears the stored path. Call it after processing the file to avoid reprocessing.
win_example1_desc: Minimal setup: window, main loop with FPS cap and custom icon.
win_example2_desc: One of the first things you'll notice when building any game is that movement feels inconsistent - too fast on some machines, too slow on others. This example solves exactly that. A green square sits at the center of the screen and moves with the arrow keys, but instead of moving a fixed amount each frame, it multiplies the speed by GetDeltaTime(). That small multiplication is what keeps things consistent at 300 pixels per second whether you're running at 30 FPS or 120. SetTargetFPS(60) is there too, but the movement doesn't rely on it.
win_example3_desc: Two windows share the same OpenGL context. The secondary window inherits the shaders and resources from the primary one. Useful for editor tools, secondary views or debug windows.
win_example3_callout: The secondary window does not reload GLAD or recompile the basic shaders; it inherits them from sharedContext.
win_example1_callout: By default, the window icon is Leak, a charming little ghost with soft blue tones that represents the spirit of the engine. Small, endearing, and perfectly readable at 16x16 pixels without losing its shape. It is hardcoded directly into the binary as an RGBA array. No paths, no stbi_load.
win_example4_desc: SetClipboardString writes a string directly into the system clipboard, making it available to any other application. GetClipboardString reads whatever is currently in the clipboard and returns it as a const char*. IsFileDropped returns true the frame a file is dragged and dropped onto the window. GetLastDroppedPath retrieves the full path of that file as a string. ClearDroppedPath resets the stored path so the engine stops reporting a drop.
api_gamepad_available: Checks whether a gamepad is connected and available.
api_gamepad_name: Retrieves the name of the connected gamepad.
api_gamepad_pressed: Detects whether a button was pressed during the current frame.
api_gamepad_released: Detects whether a button was released during the current frame.
api_gamepad_down: Checks whether a button remains pressed.
api_gamepad_up: Checks whether a button remains released.
api_gamepad_axis: Retrieves the current value of an analog axis in the range [-1.0, 1.0].
api_gamepad_axis_delta: Retrieves the change of an analog axis relative to the previous frame.
api_gamepad_axis_deadzone: Retrieves an axis value with a configurable deadzone applied.
api_gamepad_left_stick: Retrieves the left stick position with deadzone applied.
api_gamepad_right_stick: Retrieves the right stick position with deadzone applied.
api_gamepad_left_trigger: Retrieves the normalized value of the left trigger in the range [0.0, 1.0].
api_gamepad_right_trigger: Retrieves the normalized value of the right trigger in the range [0.0, 1.0].
api_gamepad_connected: True only on the frame the gamepad was connected.
api_gamepad_disconnected: True only on the frame the gamepad was disconnected.
welcome_desc: This documentation corresponds to version 2.0 of DarkMoon Engine, a new iteration compared to the one originally used in Two Wonders. Its main focus is 2D: the entire graphics system is built around primitives, textures, and a camera designed specifically for that purpose. Alongside the graphics module, the engine also includes its own ECS (Entity-Component-System), a lightweight audio module built on top of miniaudio, and a set of utils (colors, input, math and memory viewer) that support the rest of the systems.
helloworld_desc: The minimal program to open a window and enter the main loop. The starting point for any project using the engine.
install_desc: All the information about the installation is available on Github.
libraries_desc: External dependencies used internally by DarkMoon Engine. No manual setup is required; they are bundled with the engine.
lib_glad_desc: OpenGL extension loader. Provides access to graphics API functions without relying on the operating system.
lib_glfw_desc: Cross-platform window management, OpenGL context creation, and input event handling.
lib_glm_desc: Math library for graphics: vectors, matrices, and transformations compatible with OpenGL conventions.
lib_stb_desc: Single-header libraries for image loading (stb_image) and TrueType font rendering (stb_truetype).
monitor_desc: Access information about available monitors: native resolution, refresh rate, and screen selection for fullscreen mode.
camera2d_desc: 2D camera that transforms world space to screen space. Supports translation, zoom, and rotation. Passed to draw() to apply the transformation.
pixel_desc: Draws a single pixel at a given position with a solid colour. The most basic primitive in the engine.
line_desc: Draws a line between two points. Supports configurable thickness and colour.
triangle_desc: Draws a triangle defined by three vertices. Can be filled or wireframe.
rectangle_desc: Draws an axis-aligned or rotated rectangle. Supports fill, outline, and a configurable transform origin.
circle_desc: Draws a circle with a centre and radius. Configurable segment count, fill, and colour.
regular_polygon_desc: Draws a regular N-sided polygon. A generalisation of the circle useful for triangles, hexagons, and other geometric shapes.
resourcemanager_desc: Centralised cache for graphical resources. Avoids loading the same file more than once and manages the lifetime of textures and fonts.
text_desc: Text rendering via TrueType fonts. Includes a built-in embedded font and support for external fonts loaded through ResourceManager.
texture_desc: Load and draw images on screen. Supports source region (sprite sheet), scale, rotation, and colour tint.
animatedtexture_desc: GIF-based animated texture. Automatically manages frames and the timing between them.
tileset_desc: Splits a texture into uniform cells and allows drawing individual tiles by index. Foundation for level maps and tiled backgrounds.
fmod_desc: Integration with the FMOD audio engine. Load and play sounds, effects, and music with control over volume, panning, and channels.
colors_desc: Predefined colours available in the engine.
keys_desc: Keyboard key constants, mouse buttons, and gamepad buttons used in Window input queries.
math_desc: Engine math utilities: Vector2D with full operator overloading, interpolation, clamp, and common geometric functions.
memory_desc: Debug tool that displays the EntityManager's internal memory usage: slotmaps, active components, and fragmentation.
supported_platforms_desc: Operating systems and environments where the engine can be compiled and run.
gp_btn_a: South face button. A on Xbox, Cross on PlayStation.
gp_btn_b: East face button. B on Xbox, Circle on PlayStation.
gp_btn_x: West face button. X on Xbox, Square on PlayStation.
gp_btn_y: North face button. Y on Xbox, Triangle on PlayStation.
gp_btn_guide: Guide button (Xbox, PS). May not be available on all controllers.
gp_btn_last: Index of the last button. Useful for loops.
gp_axis_lt: Left trigger (LT / L2). Range -1.0 (released) to +1.0 (fully pressed).
gp_axis_rt: Right trigger (RT / R2). Range -1.0 (released) to +1.0 (fully pressed).
gp_axis_last: Index of the last axis. Useful for loops.
math_vector2d_desc: Integer 2D vector. Used for pixel/grid coordinates and other whole-number quantities.
math_v2d_ctor: Constructs a vector from two integer components.
math_op_mul_scalar_int: Scales both components by an integer.
math_op_div_scalar_int: Divides both components by an integer.
math_op_muleq_comp: In-place component-wise multiplication with another vector.
math_v2d_magnitude: Vector length, computed with a constexpr Newton-Raphson square root approximation. Returns -1.0f if called on a vector representing a negative value.
math_dot_int: Dot product of the two vectors.
math_index_int: Indexed access: 0 returns x, any other value returns y (no bounds checking).
math_free_mul_int: Commutative form of scalar multiplication (int * Vector2D).
math_v2d_callout: magnitude() uses a custom constexpr Newton-Raphson approximation (sqrt_nr) instead of std::sqrt, so it can be evaluated at compile time.
math_vector2df_desc: Floating-point 2D vector. Used for world positions, velocities, directions, and anything requiring sub-unit precision.
math_v2df_ctor: Constructs a vector from two float components.
math_op_mul_scalar_float: Scales both components by a float.
math_op_div_scalar_float: Divides both components by a float.
math_op_eq_float: Epsilon-based equality comparison (compares squared distance against 1e-6f), safe for floating-point precision issues.
math_dot_float: Dot product of the two vectors.
math_v2df_normalized: Returns a unit-length vector. Returns a zero vector if the magnitude is smaller than 1e-6f, to avoid division by (near) zero.
math_index_float: Indexed access: 0 returns x, any other value returns y (no bounds checking).
math_v2df_toint: Converts to the integer-based Vector2D. Truncates decimals, does not round.
math_free_mul_float: Commutative form of scalar multiplication (float * Vector2Df).
math_v2df_callout: toInt() truncates towards zero rather than rounding - Vector2Df(1.9f, -1.9f).toInt() gives (1, -1), not (2, -2).
memory_viewer_desc: Prints a raw hexadecimal + ASCII dump of an object's memory to stdout, in the style of a classic hex editor. Intended purely as a debugging aid.
memory_ctor_obj: Captures the address and size (via sizeof) of the given object. Works with any value: structs, arrays, primitives, etc.
memory_ctor_ptr: If a pointer is passed, dumps the memory of the pointee (sizeof(*ptr) bytes at the pointed-to address), not the pointer variable itself.
memory_printmemory: Prints the header, the object's total size, and a formatted hex/ASCII dump in rows of 16 bytes.
memory_output_desc: Each row shows the address of the first byte, 16 space-separated hex bytes, and the printable ASCII representation of those bytes (non-printable bytes shown as '.'). Bytes past the end of the object on the last row are shown as '--'.
memory_callout_dangling: Only pass named variables (lvalues) to MemoryViewer. Passing a literal or a temporary expression (e.g. MemoryViewer(5) or MemoryViewer(a + b)) leaves the internal pointer dangling as soon as the constructor returns, since the temporary's lifetime is not extended past the constructor call. Calling printMemory() afterwards is undefined behavior.
memory_callout_oob: When the object's size is not a multiple of 16, the last row reads one byte past the end of the object for the ASCII column (the hex column correctly stops at the object's boundary). This is a known out-of-bounds read; it usually just shows adjacent memory but should not be relied upon.
memory_callout_size_limit: The internal byte counter is a std::uint16_t, so objects larger than 65535 bytes will wrap the counter and produce an incorrect dump past that point.
memory_callout_ansi: Output uses ANSI/VT100 color escape codes. It will render correctly in most Linux/macOS terminals and modern Windows terminals, but may show raw escape sequences if redirected to a file or run in a terminal without ANSI support.
header_audio: A lightweight wrapper around miniaudio: load a sound file once and play it, pause it, loop it, or trigger overlapping copies of it without touching the underlying audio engine directly.
audio_whatis_desc: Audio is a small RAII wrapper that loads a sound file and gives you simple playback controls. Internally it's backed by miniaudio through a shared AudioManager singleton, and it keeps a small pool of decoded voices so the same sound can overlap itself (e.g. a rapid-fire SFX).
audio_feat_pool: Voice pooling for overlapping one-shot sounds
audio_feat_singleton: Shared audio engine (AudioManager), initialized on first use
audio_feat_backend: Powered by miniaudio (WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG)
audio_setup_desc: Audio doesn't need any manual initialization. The first Audio object you construct creates the shared AudioManager (and its underlying miniaudio engine) automatically.
audio_setup_callout: AudioManager is a singleton shared by every Audio instance in the program. It is created on the first Audio() call and destroyed automatically at program exit - you never call it directly for normal playback.
audio_playback_desc: play(), stop(), pause(), setVolume() and setLooping() control an Audio object's voice pool as a whole.
audio_pause_callout: pause() currently behaves exactly like stop(): it stops every voice in the pool without saving playback position. There is no resume-from-pause - calling play() afterwards starts a fresh voice from the beginning, not where it left off.
audio_pooling_desc: Each Audio object owns a pool of poolSize independent voices, all decoded from the same file. This lets the same sound overlap itself - useful for SFX that can trigger rapidly (footsteps, hits, UI clicks).
audio_pool_memory_callout: Each voice in the pool fully decodes its own independent copy of the audio file (no shared decoded data between voices). Memory usage scales roughly linearly with poolSize. Keep poolSize small (1-2) for music or long tracks, and only raise it for short, frequently-overlapping SFX.
audio_pool_fail_callout: If a voice fails to initialize partway through building the pool (e.g. corrupt or missing file), the effective poolSize is silently truncated to however many voices did load successfully - it is not retried.
audio_api_desc: Public interface for loading and controlling a sound.
api_audio_ctor: Loads filePath via the ResourceManager and builds a pool of poolSize voices from it.
api_audio_play: Picks a free voice from the pool (or reuses the oldest one if all are busy), rewinds it, applies the current volume/looping settings, and starts it.
api_audio_stop: Stops every voice in the pool immediately.
api_audio_setvolume: Sets the volume (applied to all currently playing voices, and stored as the default for future play() calls).
api_audio_setlooping: Enables or disables looping (applied to all currently playing voices, and stored as the default for future play() calls).
api_audio_isplaying: Returns true if at least one voice in the pool is currently playing.
api_audio_ispaused: Returns true if at least one voice in the pool is currently playing.
api_audio_isloaded: Returns true if the underlying resource finished loading successfully.
audiomanager_api_desc: Singleton that owns the shared miniaudio engine used by every Audio instance. You rarely need to touch this directly - Audio handles it internally.
api_audiomanager_getinstance: Returns the singleton instance, creating (and initializing the miniaudio engine) on first call.
api_audiomanager_get: Returns a void* to the underlying ma_engine, or nullptr if the audio backend failed to initialize (e.g. no audio device found).
api_audiomanager_isinitialized: Returns whether the miniaudio engine initialized successfully.
audiomanager_callout: If AudioManager fails to initialize (no audio device available), every Audio object created afterwards silently becomes a no-op: play()/stop()/etc. do nothing, and isLoaded() returns false. Check isLoaded() after construction if you need to detect this.
audio_example1_desc: A simple sound effect triggered on a key press, with a loaded check.
audio_example2_desc: Holding the key repeatedly triggers the same sound, overlapping itself thanks to the voice pool.
audio_example2_callout: With poolSize 8, the 9th overlapping play() call while 8 are still playing will cut off the oldest voice rather than being dropped.
audio_example3_desc: Background music with looping and live volume control.
header_monitor: A lightweight, non-owning wrapper around GLFW's monitor handles: enumerate displays, query video modes and physical geometry, react to connect/disconnect events, and adjust gamma.
monitor_whatis_desc: Monitor wraps a GLFWmonitor* handle and exposes it through a small, value-like C++ object. It doesn't own or create the underlying display it's just a convenient view into information GLFW already tracks.
monitor_feat_enumerate: Enumerate the primary monitor and every connected monitor
monitor_feat_videomodes: Query supported and current video modes
monitor_feat_physical: Physical size, content scale (DPI) and virtual desktop position
monitor_feat_gamma: Read and write the monitor's gamma ramp
monitor_setup_desc: No manual setup is required. DarkMoonEngine registers the monitor callback internally, so GetPrimaryMonitor() and GetMonitors() work right away.
monitor_setup_callout: Monitor is a lightweight, non-owning wrapper around a GLFWmonitor* handle. A default-constructed Monitor() wraps nullptr always check isValid() (or just `if (monitor)`) before using one that didn't come directly from getPrimary()/getAll().
monitor_events_desc: Monitor::initCallback() registers a single GLFW monitor callback that flips two internal flags whenever any monitor connects or disconnects. wasConnected()/wasDisconnected() (and DarkMoonEngine's MonitorConnected()/MonitorDisconnected() wrappers) read and consume those flags.
api_monitor_initcallback: Registers the internal GLFW monitor callback. Called once, typically from DarkMoonEngine's constructor you normally don't need to call this yourself.
api_monitor_wasconnected: Returns true exactly once after any monitor connects, then resets to false until the next connect event.
api_monitor_wasdisconnected: Returns true exactly once after any monitor disconnects, then resets to false until the next disconnect event.
monitor_events_global_callout: wasConnected()/wasDisconnected() are global, single-consumer flags they don't tell you which monitor changed, and only the first caller in a given frame will observe true. If multiple systems poll them, only one will ever see the event.
monitor_events_dangling_callout: A GLFWmonitor* handle becomes invalid once that display disconnects. Prefer re-fetching Monitor objects via GetMonitors()/GetPrimaryMonitor() after a disconnect event rather than holding onto old Monitor instances indefinitely.
monitor_gamma_desc: Read or replace a monitor's gamma ramp, either manually via GammaRamp or by letting GLFW generate a standard curve from a single exponent.
api_monitor_getgammaramp: Reads the monitor's current gamma ramp into a GammaRamp.
api_monitor_setgammaramp: Uploads a custom gamma ramp to the monitor.
api_monitor_setgamma: Generates and applies a standard gamma curve from an exponent. 1.0 restores the default (sRGB-like) behavior.
monitor_gamma_callout: Gamma changes affect the entire screen, not just your window.
monitor_api_desc: Full reference for the Monitor class.
api_monitor_ctor: Wraps an existing GLFWmonitor* handle. Passing nullptr (the default) yields an invalid Monitor.
api_monitor_isvalid: Returns whether this object wraps a real, connected monitor.
api_monitor_operatorbool: Equivalent to isValid(), usable directly in an if-condition.
api_monitor_handle: Returns the raw GLFWmonitor*, for interop with GLFW functions not wrapped here.
api_monitor_compare: Compares the underlying GLFWmonitor* handles for equality.
api_monitor_getprimary: Returns the operating system's primary (preferred) monitor.
api_monitor_getvideomodes: Returns every video mode (resolution/bit depth/refresh rate combination) this monitor supports.
api_monitor_getcurrentvideomode: Returns the video mode currently in use.
api_monitor_getphysicalsize: Returns the monitor's physical size in millimeters, as reported by the OS/driver (not always accurate).
api_monitor_getcontentscale: Returns the DPI content scale factor (1.0 = 100%), useful for scaling UI on high-DPI displays.
api_monitor_getposition: Returns this monitor's position within the virtual desktop (the combined coordinate space of all monitors).
api_monitor_getworkarea: Returns the usable screen area, excluding OS elements like taskbars or docks.
api_monitor_getname: Returns a human-readable name for the monitor, or an empty string if GLFW couldn't provide one.
api_monitor_setuserpointer: Attaches an arbitrary user pointer to the monitor via GLFW.
api_monitor_getuserpointer: Retrieves the previously attached user pointer.
monitor_darkmoonengine_desc: DarkMoonEngine exposes the most commonly needed monitor functionality directly, so you don't have to reach for the Monitor class's static methods yourself.
monitor_types_api_desc: Small plain-data structs used by Monitor's getters. All are simple aggregates with no behavior beyond what's listed.
type_videomode_desc: Resolution (width/height), per-channel bit depth (redBits/greenBits/blueBits) and refreshRate for a single supported display mode.
type_physicalsize_desc: widthMM / heightMM: physical dimensions of the display in millimeters.
type_contentscale_desc: x / y: the monitor's DPI scale factors, for high-DPI-aware UI scaling.
type_virtualposition_desc: x / y: this monitor's origin within the OS's virtual desktop coordinate space.
type_workarea_desc: x / y / width / height: the monitor's usable area, excluding taskbars/docks/etc.
type_gammaramp_desc: red / green / blue: per-channel lookup tables. Can be built from an existing GLFWgammaramp, or as an empty ramp of a given size, and converted back via toGLFW().
camera2d_whatis_desc: Camera2D is a small, self-contained 2D transform: given a target, an offset, a zoom and a rotation, it converts points between world space and screen space. It doesn't touch OpenGL directly drawable objects (Rectangle, Line, etc.) consume it by transforming their own vertices before uploading them.
camera2d_feat_transform: Pan, zoom and rotate the 2D view via a single struct
camera2d_feat_zoom_rotation: Independent zoom and rotation (in degrees) around the target
camera2d_feat_inverse: Exact inverse transform (ScreenToWorld) for mouse picking, UI-to-world conversions, etc.
camera2d_feat_pure: Pure math, no GPU state safe to copy, store multiple cameras, or use outside rendering
camera2d_field_target: The world-space point the camera is centered on (e.g. the player's position).
camera2d_field_offset: Where target is placed on screen, in pixels. Set this to the screen's center to get a typical 'camera follows player' setup.
camera2d_field_zoom: Scale factor applied after rotation. 1.0 = no zoom, > 1.0 = zoomed in, < 1.0 = zoomed out.
camera2d_field_rotation: Rotation of the view around target, in degrees.
camera2d_offset_callout: offset defaults to (0, 0), which places the camera's target at the top-left corner of the screen. For a centered camera, set offset = { width / 2, height / 2 } once after creating the window.
camera2d_api_desc: Two pure functions that convert a single point between world space and screen space, using the camera's current target/offset/zoom/rotation.
camera2d_worldtoscreen: Converts a world-space point to screen-space pixels: subtract target, rotate, scale by zoom, then add offset.
camera2d_screentoworld: The exact inverse of WorldToScreen: subtract offset, unscale by zoom, rotate by -rotation, then add target. Useful for turning a mouse click into a world position.
camera2d_zoom_zero_callout: ScreenToWorld() divides by zoom. Setting zoom to exactly 0 produces division by zero (Inf/NaN results). Clamp zoom to a small positive minimum (e.g. 0.01f) rather than letting it reach 0.
camera2d_rotation_direction_callout: rotation uses a standard counter-clockwise rotation matrix in a y-up coordinate system. Since screen space here has Y growing downward (as in the rest of the engine's NDC conversion), a positive rotation value will visually appear to rotate clockwise on screen.
camera2d_pure_callout: Camera2D never touches OpenGL it has no draw/update/apply method. It's purely a coordinate transform that drawable objects and your own game logic call into manually.
camera2d_drawables_desc: Every drawable primitive in the engine (Rectangle, Line, etc.) follows the same convention: a camera-less Draw() and a camera-aware Draw(camera) overload.
camera2d_perf_callout: Draw(camera) rebuilds a temporary VAO/VBO/EBO from scratch on every single call (allocated and deleted within the same call), unlike Draw(), which reuses the buffers built once in Rebuild(). Drawing many objects with the camera every frame is noticeably more expensive than drawing without it.
camera2d_coords_meaning_callout: The same stored vertices mean different things depending on which overload you call: with Draw() they're treated as screen/pixel coordinates directly; with Draw(camera) they're treated as world coordinates and transformed through the camera first. Mixing the two on the same object without accounting for this will look wrong.
camera2d_example_desc: A camera that follows the player horizontally and zooms with the scroll wheel, with zoom clamped above zero.
resourcemanager_whatis_desc: ResourceManager is a singleton that owns and caches every loaded asset (shaders, textures, audio, fonts, ...) behind a common Resource base class. It's what powers Window::CreateShader(), Audio(filePath), Texture(...), and similar constructors under the hood.
resourcemanager_feat_singleton: Single shared instance for the whole program (ResourceManager::getInstance())
resourcemanager_feat_dedup: Deduplicates loads: requesting the same file path + type twice returns the same pointer
resourcemanager_feat_ownership: Owns every resource's lifetime via std::unique_ptr, and unloads them all automatically on shutdown
resourcemanager_feat_generic: Generic loadResource<T>() works with any type deriving from Resource
resourcemanager_resource_desc: Every loadable asset type (ResourceShader, ResourceTexture, ResourceAudio, ...) derives from Resource, which stores the common bookkeeping fields and exposes a small read-only interface.
api_resource_isloaded: Whether the resource finished loading successfully. loadResource<T>() checks this right after construction to decide whether to keep or discard the resource.
api_resource_getid: The ID this resource was constructed with. See the callout below about a mismatch with the ID actually used as its map key.
api_resource_getfilepath: The file path this resource was loaded from.
api_resource_getfiletype: typeid(T).hash_code() of the concrete resource type, used internally to match cache lookups by type.
api_resource_unload: Virtual, no-op by default. Derived classes override it to release their underlying handles (GPU buffers, audio voices, etc.), typically calling it from their own destructor too.
resourcemanager_resource_ctor_callout: Resource's constructor and setup() are protected: you never construct a Resource (or a derived type) directly always go through ResourceManager::loadResource<T>(), which handles ID assignment and caching for you.
resourcemanager_api_desc: Public interface for loading, retrieving and releasing resources.
api_rm_getinstance: Returns the singleton instance, creating it on first call.
api_rm_loadresource: Returns an existing resource if one with the same file path and type T is already loaded; otherwise constructs a new T(id, typeid(T).hash_code(), filePath, args...) and caches it. Returns nullptr if the new resource failed to load.
api_rm_getresource: Looks up a resource by its map key and casts it to T*. Does not verify the stored type matches T see the type-safety callout below.
api_rm_unloadresource: Erases the resource stored under the given map key, triggering its destructor (and typically its unload()).
api_rm_unloadall: Erases every loaded resource. Called automatically by ResourceManager's destructor and by DarkMoonEngine's destructor.
resourcemanager_dedup_desc: loadResource<T>() first scans all currently loaded resources for one with a matching file path and type before creating anything new.
resourcemanager_dedup_args_callout: On a cache hit, the extra constructor arguments (args...) you passed are silently ignored you get back the resource as it was originally constructed. For example, calling Audio("theme.ogg", 1) and later Audio("theme.ogg", 8) elsewhere in your code returns the SAME underlying resource with poolSize still 1; the second poolSize is never applied.
resourcemanager_dedup_typesafety_callout: The cache match requires both the file path AND typeid(T).hash_code() to match, so loading the same file as two different resource types (e.g. as a Texture and separately as a Shader) correctly creates two independent resources.
resourcemanager_idbug_title: Known issue: ID / map key mismatch
resourcemanager_idbug_desc: There's an off-by-one between the ID a resource reports about itself and the key it's actually stored under in ResourceManager's internal map.
resourcemanager_idbug_callout: getIDResource() always returns one less than the map key the resource is actually stored under (the resource is constructed with the current nextID, which is then incremented before being used as the map key). Calling unloadResource(resource->getIDResource()) or getResource<T>(resource->getIDResource()) will therefore target the wrong entry either a neighboring resource, or nothing at all if the ID happens to be 0. Avoid round-tripping through getIDResource() for lookups/unloads until this is fixed upstream; keep the T* you got back from loadResource() instead.
resourcemanager_example_desc: Requesting the same shader twice returns the same cached pointer.
pixel_ctor: Constructs a pixel at the given position, with the given color and size. shader is optional; if omitted, the basic solid-color shader is used.
pixel_setsize: Changes the size (in pixels) of the square drawn to represent the pixel.
shape_setshader: Replaces the shader used to draw the shape.
shape_getters: Returns the current value of the corresponding property.
shape_draw: Draws the shape. The camera overload applies the Camera2D transform before rendering.
shape_delete: Releases the GPU resources (VAO/VBO/EBO) associated with the shape.
shapes_default_ctor_callout: This shape has no default constructor; all of its parameters are required at construction.
pixel_size_callout: size determines the side length (in pixels) of the square drawn to represent the pixel, not a single screen pixel.
line_ctor: Constructs a line between startPosition and endPosition, with the given color and width. shader is optional.
line_setposition: Updates the line's start and end points.
line_setwidth: Changes the line's width in pixels.
line_width_callout: Width is applied uniformly along the whole line; very large widths can distort corners on connected lines.
triangle_ctor: Constructs a triangle from its three vertices and the given color. shader is optional.
triangle_setposition: Moves the triangle by translating all three vertices together, preserving its shape.
triangle_no_default_ctor_callout: Triangle has no default constructor: all three vertices and the color must be supplied at creation.
triangle_lines_desc: Wireframe variant of Triangle: draws only the triangle's three edges instead of filling it.
triangle_lines_ctor: Constructs a triangle outline from its three vertices, color, and line width. shader is optional.
triangle_lines_getedge: Returns a pointer to the internal Line object representing that edge of the triangle.
triangle_lines_edge_callout: The pointers returned by GetEdgeAB/BC/CA point to the object's internal lines; they remain valid as long as the TriangleLines exists, but become invalid once it is destroyed.
rectangle_ctor_size: Constructs an axis-aligned rectangle from its position (top-left corner), width, and height.
rectangle_ctor_verts: Constructs a (potentially rotated) rectangle from its four explicit vertices A, B, C, and D.
rectangle_setposition: Moves the rectangle by translating all of its vertices, preserving its size and orientation.
rectangle_setsize: Changes the rectangle's width and/or height, recalculating its vertices.
rectangle_camera_perf_callout: Draw(camera) rebuilds GPU buffers on every call; for many rectangles per frame, prefer Draw() without a camera whenever possible.
rectangle_lines_desc: Wireframe variant of Rectangle: draws only the outline instead of filling it.
rectangle_lines_ctor: Constructs a rectangle outline from position, width, height, color, and line width. shader is optional.
rectangle_lines_getedge: Returns a pointer to the internal Line object representing that edge of the rectangle.
circle_ctor: Constructs a circle with the given center, radius, and color. segments controls the smoothness of the outline; shader is optional.
circle_setters: Updates the circle's center, radius, or segment count.
circle_segments_callout: More segments produce a smoother circle at the cost of more vertices; 64 is a good balance for most on-screen sizes.
circle_lines_desc: Wireframe variant of Circle: draws only the outline instead of filling it.
circle_lines_ctor: Constructs a circle outline with the given center, radius, color, segments, and line width. shader is optional.
circle_lines_setters: Updates the outline's center, radius, segment count, or line width.
regularpolygon_ctor: Constructs a regular polygon with the given center, radius, side count, and color. rotation is optional; the sentinel value -1000.0f means no explicit rotation was specified.
regularpolygon_setters: Updates the polygon's center, radius, side count, or rotation.
regularpolygon_rotation_sentinel_callout: -1000.0f is an internal sentinel value meaning 'no explicit rotation', not an actual angle; pass 0.0f (or another valid value) if you want to control rotation from the start.
regularpolygon_lines_desc: Wireframe variant of RegularPolygon: draws only the outline instead of filling it.
regularpolygon_lines_ctor: Constructs a regular polygon outline with center, radius, sides, color, rotation, and line width. rotation uses the same -1000.0f sentinel value as RegularPolygon.
regularpolygon_lines_setters: Updates the outline's center, radius, side count, rotation, or line width.
text_ctor: Loads the font at fontPath through the ResourceManager and prepares the text to be drawn at pixelHeight. shader is optional.
text_settext: Changes the text content to display.
text_setscale: Scales the text without reloading the font or changing pixelHeight.
text_getters: Returns the current value of the corresponding property.
text_unload: Releases the text's GPU resources (VAO/VBO). Called automatically from the destructor.
text_measuretext: Returns the width in pixels of the current text at the current scale. The camera overload multiplies the result by camera.zoom.
text_gettextheight: Returns the height in pixels of the current text at the current scale. The camera overload multiplies the result by camera.zoom.
text_default_ctor_callout: Unlike the basic shapes, Text does have a default constructor. A default-constructed Text has no font or window bound: it must not be used (Draw(), Unload(), MeasureText()...) until replaced with one built from the full constructor.
text_pixelheight_callout: pixelHeight sets the resolution the font atlas is generated at, at load time; it can't be changed afterward without recreating the Text object. To change the visual size at runtime, use SetScale() instead.
text_camera_measure_callout: MeasureText(camera) and GetTextHeight(camera) return the result multiplied by camera.zoom, useful for centering or aligning text drawn with Draw(camera).
texture_ctor: Loads the image at texturePath through the ResourceManager and constructs the texture with the given position, scale, and rotation. shader is optional.
texture_setrotation: Updates the element's rotation, in degrees.
texture_settexture: Replaces the currently loaded image while keeping the rest of the transform (position, scale, rotation, color).
texture_setopacity: Adjusts opacity by modifying only the alpha channel of the current color; leaves RGB unchanged.
texture_getters: Returns the current value of the corresponding property.
texture_getsize: Returns the texture's width, height, or size, already multiplied by the current scale.
texture_getrawsize: Returns the image's original dimensions in pixels, without applying the scale.
texture_getopacity: Returns the current opacity, computed as color.a / 255.
texture_rotation_todo_callout: SetRotation() is internally marked as a TODO (transform matrix); it's worth verifying that rotation is applied correctly before relying on it in production.
texture_hotswap_callout: SetTexture() replaces the loaded image but keeps the object's current position, scale, rotation, and color.
texture_opacity_callout: Opacity is stored in the alpha channel of the internal color; SetOpacity() and GetOpacity() are shortcuts that only touch that channel.
animatedtexture_ctor: Loads the animation (GIF) at texturePath through the ResourceManager and constructs the animated texture with the given position, scale, and rotation. shader is optional.
animatedtexture_update: Advances the animation by the given deltaTime. Must be called once per frame for playback to progress.
animatedtexture_playback: Play() resumes playback, Pause() stops it without resetting the current frame, and Reset() jumps back to the first frame and resumes playback.
animatedtexture_setframe: Jumps directly to the frame at the given index.
animatedtexture_setlooping: Enables or disables looping when the animation reaches the last frame.
animatedtexture_setspeed: Multiplies the playback speed (1.0 = normal, 0.5 = half speed, 2.0 = double speed).
animatedtexture_getters: Returns the current value of the corresponding property.
animatedtexture_moveonly_callout: AnimatedTexture is not copyable (its copy constructor and copy assignment operator are deleted), only movable. Store it in move-only-friendly containers (std::vector, std::unique_ptr) and avoid implicit copies.
animatedtexture_update_callout: If Update(dt) isn't called every frame, the animation stays frozen on the current frame even though IsPlaying() still returns true.
animatedtexture_speed_callout: SetSpeed() accepts any positive multiplier to speed up or slow down the animation; negative values aren't explicitly supported by the current implementation.
tileset_ctor: Loads the image at texturePath through the ResourceManager and slices it into a cols x rows grid of tileW x tileH pixel cells each. shader is optional.
tileset_getdims: Returns the cell size, the number of columns/rows, or the total tile count (cols * rows).
tileset_gettransform: Returns the scale, rotation, or color applied to every tile drawn from this TileSet.
tileset_getscaledsize: Returns a tile's width or height, already multiplied by the current scale.
tileset_draw: Draws the given tile (by column/row or by linear index) at the given screen position.
tileset_draw_camera: Same as Draw(), but applying the Camera2D transform before rendering.
tileset_index_callout: index and (col, row) are equivalent ways of referring to the same tile: index is computed internally as row * cols + col. Use whichever is more convenient for the context.
tileset_const_callout: All Draw() overloads are const: drawing tiles does not modify the TileSet's internal state.
prototype_desc: A gameplay prototype built with DarkMoon Engine, inspired by the original The Legend of Zelda on the NES. It's used to validate and demonstrate the engine's core systems while recreating the feel of a classic retro top-down adventure.
prototype_feat_topdown: Top-down gameplay inspired by classic NES adventure games
prototype_feat_debug: Debug menu for control in entities and systems
